answer: The mesa multiplier is published, charged in orchard, and sable lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4151 identities would post 4406 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
